channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: FANAC restores a 1963 SFPA mailing with nine complete fanzines
item.description: The newly updated index for Southern Fandom Press Alliance mailing 10 opens 124 scanned pages from December 1963. The nine contributions include work by Rick Norwood, Dave Hulan, Bill Plott and Larry Montgomery, making an early slice of Southern fan publishing directly browsable.

item.title: St. Augustine’s oldest house reveals layers of Florida history
item.description: A News4JAX visit to the Ximenez-Fatio House and St. Augustine Historical Society traces more than 450 years of the city’s past, from Pedro Menéndez and Spanish rule through British occupation, territorial Florida and statehood.

item.title: Composable Script Includes can make ServiceNow code smaller and faster
item.description: Andy Halstead shows how ServiceNow’s server-side JavaScript libraries can be organized as small, composable functions. The approach reduces repeated class setup, encourages explicit dependencies and offers a practical route to reusable code in a constrained runtime.

item.title: A 1945 profile captures the publishing empire behind Captain Marvel
item.description: Time's wartime profile found Fawcett publishing 14 magazines under paper rationing, after once juggling 63. It records Captain Marvel as the company's leading comic hero, notes circulation of 4.4 million comic books a month and describes the formulas behind its larger magazine business.

item.title: Matt Neuburg preserves a practical map to learning UserTalk
item.description: Neuburg's Frontier resource page points to the complete online Definitive Guide, beginner UserTalk tutorials and RubyFrontier. He calls the out-of-print O'Reilly book the best surviving route into the language while warning that some links and platform details are dated.

item.title: A duplicate-submission guide separates browser locks from server guarantees
item.description: The guide recommends one form-level submit handler, a synchronous in-flight lock and a disabled button for user feedback. It also explains why retries and multiple tabs require durable server-side idempotency when duplicate side effects cannot be tolerated.

item.title: AC Comics traces Femforce from mail-order fanzines to issue 200
item.description: AC Comics recounts Bill Black's path from 1969 mail-order Paragon publications to the 1980s direct market and the long-running Femforce. The company survived the independent-comics glut, returned the series to color and published issue 200 in 2023.

item.title: ServiceNow explains how multiple transform maps expand import-set rows
item.description: The current transform-map documentation notes that one import-set row is created per map and that selected maps run against the same set in a defined order. It also reviews reference-field costs, direct scripted assignment and event-script contexts.

item.title: Walter Koenig discusses the writing life beyond Chekov
item.description: In a wide-ranging interview tied to his memoir, Koenig talks about Hollywood, social responsibility and the pleasure of writing. His books include the filming journal Chekov's Enterprise, memoirs and the science-fiction novel Buck Alice and the Actor-Robot.

item.title: How Dynamite’s public-domain Tarzan comics ended in a licensed settlement
item.description: A comics-law analysis revisits the dispute over Dynamite’s Lord of the Jungle and Warlord of Mars. The case ended before a ruling: Dynamite argued the source novels were public domain, then settled and obtained licenses covering Tarzan and John Carter.

item.title: Restic explains how full snapshots share deduplicated backup data
item.description: Restic stores each snapshot as a complete view while uploading only changed chunks. Deleting an older snapshot does not break newer ones because snapshot metadata points to shared repository data; pruning removes chunks no remaining snapshot needs.

item.title: File 770 rounds up new robot fiction, comics and a November reading
item.description: Mike Glyer’s latest Pixel Scroll collects comics links and previews a Fantastic Fiction at KGB event with James Patrick Kelly and Stephanie Feldman. Kelly’s new collection gathers 30 years of robot stories, while Feldman has a new short-story collection.

item.title: St. Augustine’s Ximenez-Fatio House wins $750,000 preservation grant
item.description: The 1798 coquina house will receive a three-year National Park Service grant for interior and exterior preservation. The museum interprets Spanish, Minorcan, colonial and 228 years of African American history, with archaeology reaching back to pre-Columbian times.

item.title: The XML-RPC spec’s timezone answer is still a warning for implementors
item.description: Dave Winer’s compact XML-RPC specification leaves dateTime.iso8601 timezone assumptions to each server’s documentation. That small ambiguity explains why compatible implementations still need an explicit convention rather than silently treating timestamps as local time or UTC.

item.title: Public Domain Day guide maps the tangled rights inside classic characters
item.description: Duke’s 2026 guide separates expired copyrights, unrenewed works, later protected additions and trademarks. Its Betty Boop and Mickey examples show why a character can be free to reuse in one form while later plots, dialogue or designs remain protected.
item.source: Center for the Study of the Public Domain
